Latch

Mechanical admission gates for small-model reasoning

  1. What it is
  2. What exists
  3. What was measured
  4. What was not measured or built
  5. Known weaknesses and negative results
  6. Open questions
  7. Evidence

What it is

  • The Latch pilot, a typed-operator admission gate against free chain-of-thought on multi-hop QA, was killed at its preregistered G3 gate: the gated arm scored 37.5% at full coverage against 80.6% for chain-of-thought. #latch-pilot-killed
  • A preregistered provenance gate for small-model tool calls cut wrong state-changing actions at every model size, but cost more task success and correct actions than the registered margins allowed, so the verdict was null. #latch-study3-agent-gate

What exists

#latch-paper BUILT LINKED as of 2026-11-11

I wrote a paper draft reporting the Latch negative result: 'When Gates Abstain Too Often: Typed Operator Gates Fail to Beat Chain-of-Thought on Multi-Hop QA'.

Does not show
Submission, review or publication. Status beyond 'draft' is unknown. The worktree has an untracked paper/ directory not read in the walk.

What was measured

What was not measured or built

#latch-gated-slm-chain DESIGN-ONLY AUTHOR-REPORTED as of 2026-11-17

A gated chain of small language models (GIN's sole-writer gate pointed inward at inference steps) is a hypothesis only; no multi-model arm has been run.

Verification
Author-reported, not re-verified. No tier-1 artifact containing this claim was opened for this site.
Does not show
Any result for free-form SLM chains vs gated SLM chains vs one SLM at equal token budget. The Latch pilot and study 3 tested single-model gates only. The sprawl note the seed points to was not found: the Sprawl folder on disk is empty.
Sources disagree
The seed describes a three-arm experiment. HISTORY.md records a five-arm design (single CoT, free multi-SLM, single + gate, multi + gate + agreement, self-consistency). Neither has been run in its multi-model form. These are related to, but not the same work as, latch-pilot-killed and latch-study3-agent-gate.
Evidence
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : docs/HISTORY.md tier 2 — origin 2026-11-06; 5-arm design incl. multi-SLM arms 1 and 3
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : PREREG.md tier 2 — section 2: 'multi-model arms 1/3 excluded by scope'
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : study3/RESULTS.md tier 2 — arms A0-A3 are all single-model

What each entry's evidence does not show

  • #latch-paper Submission, review or publication. Status beyond 'draft' is unknown. The worktree has an untracked paper/ directory not read in the walk.
  • #latch-gated-slm-chain Any result for free-form SLM chains vs gated SLM chains vs one SLM at equal token budget. The Latch pilot and study 3 tested single-model gates only. The sprawl note the seed points to was not found: the Sprawl folder on disk is empty.
  • #latch-pilot-killed Anything about gates that anchor to literal artifacts (fetched bytes, export rows). It tests a model translating a free-form question into a formal schema. Scoring was manual and not blinded; few-shot Example 5 was written from errors in the same 72 questions, which makes Arm 2's number optimistic; and PREREG section 5 treats abstentions as 'not answered, never wrong' while the headline scores them as wrong. The kill clause holds under either reading.
  • #latch-study2-agreement Compositional questions (excluded; the gate admitted 0 of 25 there in Phase 1). One model, one benchmark.
  • #latch-study3-agent-gate Whether a warning instead of a block, or exempting values the model could look up, would keep the catch without the false alarms. That needs a new registered study. One benchmark, one model family, one decoding setting; the audit had one labeller.

Known weaknesses and negative results

#latch-pilot-killed KILLED LINKED as of 2026-11-11

The Latch pilot, a typed-operator admission gate against free chain-of-thought on multi-hop QA, was killed at its preregistered G3 gate: the gated arm scored 37.5% at full coverage against 80.6% for chain-of-thought.

Reported numbers
Numbers for latch-pilot-killed
MetricValuen / denominatorDatasetSyntheticSystemDate
accuracy at full coverage, Arm 0 (CoT) vs Arm 2 (gate)80.6% vs 37.5% (-43.1 pp)58/72 vs 27/722WikiMultihopQA validation, annotated-decomposable subset of a 100-question stratified samplenoqwen2.5:14b, v4 prompts2026-11-11

Kill criterion
PREREG.md, G3: promote only if Arm 2 beats Arm 0 by >= 15 pp at full coverage with p < 0.05 (McNemar); kill if Arm 2 loses to Arm 0.
Does not show
Anything about gates that anchor to literal artifacts (fetched bytes, export rows). It tests a model translating a free-form question into a formal schema. Scoring was manual and not blinded; few-shot Example 5 was written from errors in the same 72 questions, which makes Arm 2's number optimistic; and PREREG section 5 treats abstentions as 'not answered, never wrong' while the headline scores them as wrong. The kill clause holds under either reading.
Sources disagree
The McNemar statistic on the 32 jointly answered questions (b=4, c=2) appears as chi2 = 0.167 in POSTMORTEM.md and the vault, and as chi2 = 0.67, p = 0.41 in paper.tex. Both come from the same cells; the site builder's reading is that one uses a continuity correction, which the author has not confirmed. Neither changes the kill.
Evidence
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : docs/POSTMORTEM.md tier 1 — committed version; the worktree has uncommitted edits to this file, not used here
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : PREREG.md tier 1 — G3 promote/kill criteria; unchanged since 37b8a9c
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : LOG.md tier 1 — G3 KILL entry, commit 4adbb01
Notes
Stage history from POSTMORTEM: G1 promoted (74/100 decomposable; re-annotation 72/100, kappa 0.949). G2 was killed under the strict gate (0% admit), the gate and prompts were redesigned, G2 was killed again on manual review (16 of 26 non-trivial admits structurally valid but semantically wrong), then promoted at about 50% correct formalization with v4 prompts. G3 then killed the pilot.

#latch-study2-agreement NEGATIVE-RESULT LINKED as of 2026-11-16

In a preregistered follow-up on 600 questions, gate/chain-of-thought agreement flagged chain-of-thought errors, but no better than plain self-consistency, so the gate added nothing over resampling.

Open questions

  • Does mechanical admission pay off only when a claim can be anchored to a literal artifact? from #latch-pilot-killed
    Would resolve it: A registered test on a gate that anchors to fetched bytes or export rows.
  • Would a warning, or exempting values the model could look up, keep the catch without the false alarms? from #latch-study3-agent-gate
    Would resolve it: A new registered study (named in study 3's limitations).
  • Does a gated chain of small models behave differently from one gated model? from #latch-gated-slm-chain
    Would resolve it: Running the multi-model arms, which no study so far has.
